# Tailfuse

> Tailfuse connects one machine to several Tailscale tailnets at once. It runs one userspace Tailscale node per tailnet and a loopback router on 127.0.0.1:43100 that sends each hostname to the tailnet that owns it. It is a menu-bar app and a `tailfuse` command-line tool for macOS, Windows and Linux. Free for two tailnets; a license key for more is by optional donation, from $0.

Tailfuse is made by Ailio Technologies Inc. (https://ailio.ca). It is an independent tool, not affiliated with or endorsed by Tailscale Inc. The source is MIT licensed. `tailscaled` and `tailscale` are separate Tailscale binaries under the Tailscale terms.

## What it does

- Several tailnets online at once: no VM, no account switching, no second full Tailscale daemon.
- Each tailnet runs in userspace networking mode (`tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking`): no TUN device, no routes, no DNS changes. An installed Tailscale client keeps its primary tailnet.
- One local router on `127.0.0.1:43100` speaks SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT and serves a PAC file at `http://127.0.0.1:43100/tailfuse.pac`.
- Routing is by hostname suffix. Each profile owns suffixes such as `.work.ts.net`; the longest match wins.
- A hostname no profile owns is refused, never sent to another tailnet. Browsers using the PAC file connect direct for those names.
- Tunnels pin a local port to one tailnet service, for example `127.0.0.1:5432` to `db.work.ts.net:5432`.
- Keys are locked to the user's account: each tailnet's node keys and control socket sit in a folder only that account can open; auth keys and the license key are kept in the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager, not in the config file (on Linux the config file is readable only by the user).
- It runs as the user: no root helper and no kernel extension. The one system setting it changes is the system's automatic proxy (PAC) address, set once with the user's permission and removable from the app's settings.

## Install

- The menu-bar app, served from GitHub Releases: https://tailfuse.com/download (picks the platform), or https://tailfuse.com/download/app/macos (universal .dmg), /download/app/windows (installer), /download/app/linux (AppImage), /download/app/linux-deb
- The command-line tool, as an archive: https://tailfuse.com/download/cli/macos, /download/cli/windows, /download/cli/linux-amd64, /download/cli/linux-arm64
- The app and the command line both run Tailscale's own `tailscaled`, which must be installed on the machine.
- macOS: `brew install ailio-technologies-inc/tap/tailfuse`
- Windows: `winget install ailio-technologies-inc.tailfuse`
- From source: `cargo install --git https://github.com/ailio-technologies-inc/tailfuse tailfuse-cli`

## Quick start

```sh
tailfuse init                      # starter config
tailfuse profile login personal    # browser sign-in, once per tailnet
tailfuse profile login work
tailfuse up                        # router + system PAC
```

Config lives at `~/.config/tailfuse/config.yaml`:

```yaml
profiles:
  personal:
    suffixes: [.home-lab.ts.net]
  work:
    suffixes: [.work.ts.net, .internal.example]
    accept_routes: true
    exit_node: exit-us
tunnels:
  - name: prod-db
    profile: work
    listen: 127.0.0.1:5432
    target: db.work.ts.net:5432
```

## Commands

- `tailfuse up [--no-pac]`: start everything and set the system PAC.
- `tailfuse down`: clear the system PAC.
- `tailfuse status`: per-profile state, hostname and Tailscale IPs.
- `tailfuse test <host>`: show which profile owns a hostname.
- `tailfuse ssh user@host.work.ts.net`: SSH through the owning profile.
- `tailfuse run curl http://wiki.work.ts.net`: run any command with the proxy environment.
- `tailfuse env`: print the proxy environment for your shell.
- `tailfuse tunnel add prod-db --listen 127.0.0.1:5432 --target db.work.ts.net:5432 --profile work`: pin a local port to a tailnet service.
- `tailfuse serve-pac`: just the PAC URL, for manual browser configuration.
- `tailfuse license activate <key>`: activate a license key.

## License keys and price

- Two tailnet profiles are free, forever.
- More profiles need a license key. The key is by optional donation: the form at https://tailfuse.com/#pricing takes any amount from $0 up, and a $0 key is the same key as a paid one.
- A key covers updates for a year, and the version you have keeps working after that.
- Keys are signed and verified offline: no phone-home, no account, no telemetry.
